newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN INVESTORS URGED TO FIGHT INEQUALITY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN INVESTORS URGED TO FIGHT INEQUALITY.

text.p: South Africa's private sector must take "creative" action to erase apartheid's legacy of inequality or else the government will step in, a special advisor to Labour Minister Tito Mboweni said on Thursday.

"As investors, as managers, you can make a major impact on inequality," David Lewis, a former British trade unionist now based at the University of Cape Town, told a meeting of the Weekend Argus-Seeff Trust investment forum.

"The gap in this country between wages on the shop floor and those of supervisors and middle managers is simply unsustainable. It's larger than anywhere in the world and something has to be done about it," Lewis said.
He said South Africa also had to move boldly to promote black ownership and affirmative action.
"The danger is that if you do not do it, then you will not lay the basis for an economy and a society capable of ensuring healthy returns on your investment," Lewis said.
He said this was a danger that threatened the whole country, which made it government's responsibility to ensure inequality was addressed.

"So if you do not think creatively about wage gaps, if you do not think creatively about affirmative action, if you do not think creatively about how to expand black ownership, then the public authority has to (act)," he said, without elaborating.
